dialect.detail: JMA ORCA (Japan Medical Association standard receipt software) running on Linux with GnuCOBOL; program ORCS01 is a patient co-payment calculation subprogram for the Japanese national health insurance receipt system
evidence: no COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS
34 COPY statements, 100 CALLs typical of GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL ORCA system

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese national health insurance (Kokuho/Shakai-hoken) medical receipt (rezept) co-payment calculation for various insurance types including elderly care, long-term care, and regional public expense subsidies
purpose.summary: ORCS01 is a large batch subprogram in the JMA ORCA medical receipt system that calculates patient co-payment amounts (futan-kin) for Japanese health insurance claims. It handles multiple insurance types, regional public expense subsidies, elderly patient thresholds, and various special calculation rules. The program has an extensive revision history spanning 2000–2008 covering numerous regulatory changes to Japanese health insurance law.

notable_features: Extremely large single file (~1.65 MB, 33044 lines)
34 COPY statements indicating heavy use of copybooks
757 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
No COMP-3 (packed decimal) usage despite financial calculations
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
Extensive Japanese-language comments (EUC-JP encoded, decoded as latin-1)
Long revision history with 100+ named revisions from 2000–2008
verdict.notes: File decoded with latin-1 but comments are actually EUC-JP encoded Japanese text (garbled in latin-1 view). This is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system. The absence of COMP-3 is notable for a financial calculation program but consistent with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL ORCA codebase conventions. Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full file is ~1.65 MB.
